scenarios.title: Repair a directory import command
scenarios.summary: Select virtual input, matching fictional credentials and a valid import operation.
scenarios.objective: Use the provided LDIF input at /work/changes.ldif to import the listed new people into ou=People,dc=orchard,dc=test. Select supplied credentials that can create these entries, and make the command name the matching identity and provided directory. All input records must run successfully in every sample. Preserve all existing entries and fields; do not replace the roster.
steps: Inspect the supplied input and actual results; repair the command or LDIF, then check every sample.
scenarios.explanation: The utility name/default determines whether entry content is added. -H selects the supplied directory, -D names the identity, -W uses the selected fictional credential profile, and -f selects the supplied virtual input. A named identity still needs matching credentials and delegated Add permission. Use actual exit status and resulting directory, not a plausible command string, to verify the import.
hints: Read the first actual failure and its record number before changing later data.
Compare the selected fictional profile with -D, the provided URI/input and the required operation.
For new entry content, ldapadd and ldapmodify -a are supported alternatives. Choose the delegated operator and the supplied input.
scenarios.simplifications: Checked2026-11-09 against LPIC-2v4.5/210.3 and OpenLDAP2.6.10 documentation/source, RFC2849/4511/4513. Bounded in-process utility, fictional source-held credential profiles, literal supported options and a single virtual input/editor buffer. Every run starts from the original selected sample; Check work repeats all samples. No host command/files/network, actual Bind/server/TLS/SASL, personal passwords, full ACL/schema, implicit default replacement, continuous mode, controls, rename, ldapdelete or password utility. The selected profile supplies the fictional -W password; the saved work stores only its key. This is narrow utility practice, not full objective coverage or real equipment experience.
solution:
LDAP CHANGE WORK

ldapadd -x -W -H ldap://directory.example.test -D 'uid=operator,ou=People,dc=orchard,dc=test' -f /work/changes.ldif

scenarios.title: Recover a stopped directory update
scenarios.summary: Diagnose a stopped batch, repair simulated records and preserve the roster.
scenarios.objective: The sample already contains uid=mina,ou=People,dc=orchard,dc=test; do not create it again. Set that existing person's complete mail list to mina@orchard.test and description to dispatch. Preserve its name, class and other fields. Create uid=noah,ou=People,dc=orchard,dc=test with cn Noah Penn, sn Penn, mail noah@orchard.test and description dispatch. Use a supplied fictional credential profile and a supported utility command. Every request must succeed; preserve every unrelated entry.
steps: Inspect the supplied input and actual results; repair the command or LDIF, then check every sample.
scenarios.explanation: The existing person makes a repeated Add fail with EntryAlreadyExists (68). Read the failure before assuming later input ran. Modify the existing optional fields, retain the Add for the new person, and choose add-default mode for its content record. A record-level error retains earlier successful requests in that run; it does not make the whole batch a transaction.
hints: Read the first actual failure and its record number before changing later data.
Compare the selected fictional profile with -D, the provided URI/input and the required operation.
An existing entry needs a supported Modify; a new content entry needs add-default mode.
scenarios.simplifications: Checked2026-11-09 against LPIC-2v4.5/210.3 and OpenLDAP2.6.10 documentation/source, RFC2849/4511/4513. Every run starts from the original selected sample; Check work repeats all samples. No host command/files/network, actual Bind/server/TLS/SASL, personal passwords, full ACL/schema, implicit default replacement, continuous mode, controls, rename, ldapdelete or password utility.
